emergencyNumbers.note: The Dutch advice also lists 241162, 241163 and 241164 as general emergency numbers.

emergencyNumbers.note: Listed in the Dutch travel advice without an area code; check how to dial it from a mobile phone.

emergencyNumbers.note: Listed in the Dutch travel advice without an area code; check how to dial it from a mobile phone.

facts.title: Visa required
facts.body: Apply for a tourist e-visa at laoevisa.gov.la before you go — it only works at specific ports (see Entry). Some airports and borders issue a visa on arrival.

facts.title: Visa on arrival: bring USD and a photo
facts.body: Per travel guides: about US$30–42 depending on nationality, paid in US dollars, plus a 4×6 cm passport photo; a small overtime fee applies outside office hours. Check the official checkpoint list.

sources.title: Laos visa and entry requirements — Rough Guides

facts.title: Passport ≥6 months on departure, 2 blank pages
facts.body: Valid for at least 6 months when you leave Laos, with at least 2 blank pages.

facts.title: Laos Digital Immigration Form (LDIF)
facts.body: Fill in within 3 days before arrival and again within 3 days before departure, at the Immigration Department site. Keep the QR code offline.

sources.title: Laos Digital Immigration Form — Immigration Department

facts.title: Orange: Xaysomboune and the Myanmar border (Bokeo)
facts.body: Rebels are active in Xaysomboune — stay on main roads, don't travel after dark. Armed gangs around the Laos–Myanmar border in Bokeo and the Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone.

facts.title: Methanol poisoning
facts.body: Tourists died in Vang Vieng in Nov 2024 after drinking alcohol likely contaminated with methanol. No free drinks; only from sealed bottles or cans — everywhere in Laos.

facts.title: Drink spiking and robbery
facts.body: Foreigners are sometimes drugged in bars or taxis and then robbed or assaulted. Keep your food and drink in sight.

facts.title: "Happy" menus in Vang Vieng
facts.body: Some bars sell drug-laced "happy" or "special" items; people working with police offer drugs to trap tourists.

facts.title: Unexploded ordnance
facts.body: Xiang Khouang and Luang Prabang provinces, and along the Vietnam border (Attapeu, Sekong, Salavan, Savannakhet, south Khammouane). Don't leave main roads.

facts.title: Monsoon May–October
facts.body: Landslides and mudflows damage roads; water-sport accidents around Vang Vieng, some fatal.

facts.title: No Dutch embassy in Laos
facts.body: The Dutch embassy in Bangkok covers Laos (+66 2 309 5200); there is an honorary consul in Vientiane. 24/7: +31 247 247 247.

facts.title: Very limited healthcare
facts.body: Basic care in Vientiane; almost no reliable care elsewhere. Serious cases need evacuation abroad — your insurance must cover it. GGD: dengue, chikungunya, malaria, rabies.

facts.title: Drugs
facts.body: Soft drugs included; up to life or death penalty. One ecstasy pill for own use already means life imprisonment.

facts.title: Vapes and shisha banned
facts.body: Using, possessing or importing them: high fine and prison.

facts.title: Always carry your passport
facts.body: Authorities can ask for it; a high fine if you don't have it. Keep a photo of it on your phone too.

facts.title: No card or dice games in public
facts.body: They can be treated as gambling: high fine.

facts.title: Temples
facts.body: No public affection on or around temple grounds — you can be arrested and deported.

facts.title: No photos of military, police or protests
facts.body: Risk of arrest or prison.

facts.title: Relationships with Lao nationals
facts.body: Sexual relations between unmarried foreigners and Lao nationals are prohibited: fine or prison.

facts.title: Driving needs an IDP
facts.body: A Dutch licence is only valid together with a valid IDP.

facts.title: Laos–China Railway
facts.body: Vientiane – Vang Vieng – Luang Prabang – Boten. Tickets in the official LCR Ticket app; domestic sales open about 7 days ahead and sell out fast in Dec–Feb. Station security bans aerosols and knives.

facts.title: No Grab in Laos
facts.body: Grab does not operate in Laos (it lists eight other Southeast Asian countries). Use tuk-tuks or local ride apps and agree prices first.

facts.title: Plugs: A, B, C, E, F; 230 V
facts.body: Mains is 230 V / 50 Hz. Dutch round-pin plugs usually fit; bring a universal adapter anyway.
